item.title: [Transaction] Kevin Porter (ORL): ESPN’s Shams Charania reports Kevin Porter Jr. is finalizing a two-year contract with the Orlando Magic.
item.description:
ESPN’s Shams Charania reports Kevin Porter Jr. is finalizing a two-year contract with the Orlando Magic.

Porter was waived by the Bucks in October. The 26-year-old guard also met with the Nuggets before deciding to sign with the Magic this week, according to Charania. Porter figures to provide Orlando with backcourt depth. He averaged 17.4 points, 5.2 rebounds and 7.4 assists last season.

Nick Shlain

item.title: [Recap] Christian Braun (DEN): Christian Braun notched 15 points (5-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Mavericks.
item.description:
Christian Braun notched 15 points (5-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Mavericks.

Braun recorded a full stat line on Tuesday, and he continues to provide top-100 fantasy value. He’s reached double figures in scoring in seven straight games and has been a top-50 player over the last two weeks. After a subpar 2025-26 season in which he played a career-low 44 games, Braun has rebounded nicely. And given the lack of production from Denver’s bench, there are likely to be even more opportunities for Braun to make some things happen as a scorer.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Cameron Johnson (DEN): Cameron Johnson accounted for 17 points (5-of-15 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, three assists and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Mavericks.
item.description:
Cameron Johnson accounted for 17 points (5-of-15 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, three assists and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Mavericks.

Matching his season-high with four three-pointers, Johnson is 8-of-16 from beyond the arc over his last two games. His overall field-goal percentage against the Mavericks wasn’t good, but fantasy managers should be encouraged that Johnson kept shooting instead of passing up looks. Unfortunately, Johnson didn’t record any defensive stats, but he is averaging 1.2 steals per game.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Jamal Murray (DEN): Jamal Murray accumulated 20 points (6-of-17 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Mavericks.
item.description:
Jamal Murray accumulated 20 points (6-of-17 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Mavericks.

After torching the Bulls for 45 points on Sunday, Murray cooled off considerably on Tuesday. The Mavericks certainly deserve credit, as their defense throughout the night made life difficult for Murray individually and the Nuggets as a whole. He’s scored at least 20 points in seven of his last eight games, so one bad night isn’t enough to sound the alarm. Murray will look to bounce back on Friday against the Jazz.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Nikola Jokić (DEN): Nikola Jokić finished Tuesday’s loss to the Mavericks with 18 points (6-of-14 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), 11 rebounds, five assists, one steal and one three-pointer.
item.description:
Nikola Jokić finished Tuesday’s loss to the Mavericks with 18 points (6-of-14 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), 11 rebounds, five assists, one steal and one three-pointer.

Jokić recorded his 13th double-double of the season, but this was far from a vintage performance for the three-time MVP. He committed five turnovers, the most in a game for The Joker since recording seven in a November 16 loss to the Suns. Jokić remains among the most valuable players in fantasy basketball regardless of format, but he’s come back to the pack somewhat after multiple seasons of dominance.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Caleb Martin (DAL): Caleb Martin tallied 13 points (5-of-8 FGs), four rebounds, four assists, five steals, two blocks and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Nuggets.
item.description:
Caleb Martin tallied 13 points (5-of-8 FGs), four rebounds, four assists, five steals, two blocks and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Nuggets.

Rostered in 11 percent of Yahoo leagues, Martin finished Tuesday’s victory with a stat line that will make fantasy managers take notice. He recorded a career-high five steals, along with two blocked shots, while also shooting well from the field and beyond the arc. Martin has nine steals over his last two games and has recorded multiple steals in four of his last five appearances. The only negative is that Dallas plays only one more game this week, Friday in Phoenix.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] P.J. Washington (DAL): P.J. Washington (illness) recorded 14 points (6-of-11 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Nuggets.
item.description:
P.J. Washington (illness) recorded 14 points (6-of-11 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Nuggets.

Washington returned to the Mavericks’ rotation after a two-game absence, but not as a starter. However, the reserve role did not negatively affect his production, and Washington still played 25 minutes. Zaccharie Risacher (12/6/1/2/1 with one three-pointer) played 21 minutes as the starter, so the rotation could change as soon as Friday’s game against the Suns.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Kyrie Irving (DAL): Kyrie Irving amassed 11 points (5-of-19 FGs), five rebounds, six assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Nuggets.
item.description:
Kyrie Irving amassed 11 points (5-of-19 FGs), five rebounds, six assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Nuggets.

Irving struggled with his shot, making one of eight three-point attempts. However, he was better offensively in the second half, dishing out five of his six assists to help the Mavericks pull away. Irving entered Tuesday shooting 45.9 percent from the field, so there shouldn’t be much concern after his 5-of-19 night against the Nuggets. Dallas ends its Week 6 with a game against the Suns on Friday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Cooper Flagg (DAL): Cooper Flagg finished Tuesday’s win over the Nuggets with 24 points (8-of-17 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), six rebounds, 12 assists and one three-pointer.
item.description:
Cooper Flagg finished Tuesday’s win over the Nuggets with 24 points (8-of-17 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), six rebounds, 12 assists and one three-pointer.

In addition to recording his sixth double-double of the season, Flagg matched his career high in steals, which he initially set in a November 8 win over the Nets. Just as impressive, the reigning Rookie of the Year committed just one turnover in 31 minutes. Flagg has provided first-round fantasy value, and he is well positioned to continue producing at a high level for the Mavericks.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Trae Young (WAS): Trae Young accounted for 17 points (4-of-9 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), 12 assists, two steals and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics.
item.description:
Trae Young accounted for 17 points (4-of-9 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), 12 assists, two steals and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics.

Young continues to take a step back as a scorer, which is by design. The Wizards want him to focus more on setting up others, and he did that very well on Tuesday. Young recorded 12 assists while committing one turnover in one of his most efficient efforts of the season. However, the issue isn’t Young shooting the ball less; it’s that his accuracy has taken a hit. Tuesday’s 4-of-9 effort will help, but he’s still shooting 36.8 percent from the field this season.

Raphielle Johnson

Fonte: The Athletic

item.title: [Recap] AJ Dybantsa (WAS): AJ Dybantsa finished Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics with 20 points (7-of-18 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), 11 rebounds, seven assists and two three-pointers.
item.description:

A 20-point scorer in four of his last five games, Dybantsa has recorded three double-doubles during this stretch. Add in the seven assists, and this was a good night for those rostering the rookie, even if he didn’t record any defensive stats. Dybantsa still isn’t providing top-100 per-game value, but he’s not far from that threshold.

item.title: [Recap] Ausar Thompson (DET): Ausar Thompson produced six points (3-of-3 FGs), 10 rebounds, seven assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Magic.
item.description:
Ausar Thompson produced six points (3-of-3 FGs), 10 rebounds, seven assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Magic.

While he doesn’t offer much as a scorer, Thompson’s ability to fill a stat line is what keeps his category league value in a good place. In addition to recording a season-high four blocks, the Pistons wing hit double digits in rebounds for the sixth time while also dishing out seven assists. Adding a dependable shot to his game would do wonders for Thompson’s fantasy value, but that doesn’t seem likely anytime soon.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Kevin Huerter (DET): Kevin Huerter amassed 13 points (6-of-10 FGs), six rebounds, five assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Magic.
item.description:
Kevin Huerter amassed 13 points (6-of-10 FGs), six rebounds, five assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Magic.

Since moving into the Pistons’ starting lineup following Duncan Robinson’s quad injury, Huerter has scored in double figures in three of five games. Limited to two points in Sunday’s loss to the Hawks, “Red Velvet” bounced back with a solid performance in Orlando. Huerter is rostered in 22 percent of Yahoo leagues, a fair number given his production, even with Robinson sidelined.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Isaiah Joe (DET): Isaiah Joe finished Tuesday’s win over the Magic with 21 points (8-of-15 FGs), four rebounds, one steal and five three-pointers.
item.description:
Isaiah Joe finished Tuesday’s win over the Magic with 21 points (8-of-15 FGs), four rebounds, one steal and five three-pointers.

Joe made his first start of the season on Tuesday after Cade Cunningham (knee) was scratched late. One game removed from scoring 19 points, Joe recorded his first 20-point stat line of the season, shooting 5-of-11 from beyond the arc. The Pistons host the Bucks on Friday. And while that may be enough time for Cunningham to return, there may still be value in holding onto Joe, given how much the Bucks have struggled this season.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Daniss Jenkins (DET): Daniss Jenkins recorded 15 points (6-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, 10 assists, two steals and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Magic.
item.description:
Daniss Jenkins recorded 15 points (6-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, 10 assists, two steals and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Magic.

With Cade Cunningham (knee) being a late scratch, Jenkins moved into the starting point guard role on Tuesday. While he did commit five turnovers, the third-year guard hit double digits in assists for the first time this season and the fifth time in his career. This wasn’t Jenkins’ most efficient outing, but he provided solid value in multiple categories. At a minimum, he should be rostered until Jalen Duren returns from his hamstring injury.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Jake LaRavia (LAL): Jake LaRavia recorded a double-double on Monday with 15 points (6-of-10 FGs), 10 rebounds, one assist, two steals and one three-pointer against the Jazz.
item.description:
Jake LaRavia recorded a double-double on Monday with 15 points (6-of-10 FGs), 10 rebounds, one assist, two steals and one three-pointer against the Jazz.

LaRavia returned to the starting lineup after two games as a reserve. He took advantage of the opportunity by setting a new season high for scoring and recording his first double-double of the season. LaRavia’s scoring is down from last season, but he has been a decent source of steals. However, that isn’t enough for him to be considered a must-roster player, even if this was a strong performance.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Quentin Grimes (LAL): Quentin Grimes contributed nine points (1-of-8 FGs), three rebounds, eight assists, one block and one three-pointer against the Jazz on Monday.
item.description:
Quentin Grimes contributed nine points (1-of-8 FGs), three rebounds, eight assists, one block and one three-pointer against the Jazz on Monday.

Grimes struggled with his shot in what could be his final start before Austin Reaves (heel) returns to the lineup, but he made up for it with his passing. He surpassed his season high of seven assists, which he set in his previous outing. In the three games since he scored 47 points, Grimes has scored a total of 42 points. It was a fun stretch for him as a starter, and if he gets the chance again, he’ll be worth streaming. However, initial reports had Reaves returning for either this game against Utah or for Friday’s game against the Spurs, so Grimes will likely return to a bench role in their next game.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Luka Dončić (LAL): Luka Dončić led the Lakers with 28 points (8-of-24 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists, one steal and three three-pointers in a 109-94 win over the Jazz on Monday.
item.description:
Luka Dončić led the Lakers with 28 points (8-of-24 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists, one steal and three three-pointers in a 109-94 win over the Jazz on Monday.

Dončić didn’t have his best shooting night, but he did enough to lead the Lakers in scoring and to a second straight win. They were also able to get some revenge after Utah ended their nine-game win streak last week. Dončić is still putting up strong numbers, but he has cooled off a bit after his scorching hot start to the season. They’ll take on the Spurs on Friday in what will be a battle for first place in the West.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Ace Bailey (UTA): Ace Bailey posted a full line on Monday with 18 points (8-of-16 FGs), five rebounds, one assist, two steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Lakers.
item.description:
Ace Bailey posted a full line on Monday with 18 points (8-of-16 FGs), five rebounds, one assist, two steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Lakers.

Bailey continues to provide well-rounded value in his second season, and he has shown tremendous growth. He did a little bit of everything in this game, though it wasn’t enough for Utah to get the win. Bailey will continue to be a solid producer with Lauri Markkanen (wrist) still sidelined for a while longer. He hasn’t had many big games, but he has been consistent.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Kyle Filipowski (UTA): Kyle Filipowski provided a boost off the bench with 21 points (8-of-14 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs), 12 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in a 109-94 loss to the Lakers on Monday.
item.description:
Kyle Filipowski provided a boost off the bench with 21 points (8-of-14 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs), 12 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in a 109-94 loss to the Lakers on Monday.

Filipowski wasn’t in the rotation to start the season despite Jusuf Nurkić being sidelined, which was concerning. However, he was able to take advantage of his opportunity in this game. He set season highs for points, rebounds and assists while recording his first double-double of the season. It took Nurkić and Jaxson Hayes being out for him to get minutes, so this doesn’t make him a must-add, though he’s worth keeping an eye on to see how he fits into the rotation moving forward.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Mo Bamba (UTA): Mo Bamba started on Monday and contributed six points (3-of-7 FGs), seven rebounds, two assists and two blocks against the Lakers.
item.description:
Mo Bamba started on Monday and contributed six points (3-of-7 FGs), seven rebounds, two assists and two blocks against the Lakers.

Bamba got the starting nod with Jaxson Hayes (knee) sidelined for this game. However, he wasn’t able to replicate his production from his last few games as a starter. He played 29 minutes, but he was thoroughly outplayed by Kyle Filipowski, who played less than 24 minutes off the bench. It seems Bamba’s strong stretch as a starter wasn’t actually going to lead to him being a fantasy stud for the rest of the season. Who knew?

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Zach LaVine (SAC): Zach LaVine recorded 18 points (8-of-17 FGs), six rebounds, two assists, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Spurs.
item.description:
Zach LaVine recorded 18 points (8-of-17 FGs), six rebounds, two assists, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Spurs.

On a night when backcourt partner Darius Acuff Jr. (12 points, one rebound and four assists) went 5-of-14 from the field, LaVine shot a solid percentage and scored 18 points. Since going off for 31 points in a November 10 loss to the Magic, the veteran guard has scored 19 points or less in five straight games. However, LaVine’s fantasy value remains strong, as he’s exceeded his ADP (103) by a few rounds in nine-cat formats.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] De'Andre Hunter (SAC): De’Andre Hunter amassed 15 points (7-of-12 FGs), seven rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Spurs.
item.description:
De’Andre Hunter amassed 15 points (7-of-12 FGs), seven rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Spurs.

After dishing out eight assists total in his prior three appearances, Hunter matched that number on Monday. Those eight assists were double his previous high this season, and Hunter was also valuable to fantasy managers as a scorer and rebounder. However, as has been the case for most of his NBA career, Hunter’s inability to provide defensive stats keeps his fantasy value low.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Keegan Murray (SAC): Keegan Murray accounted for 14 points (6-of-12 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Spurs.
item.description:
Keegan Murray accounted for 14 points (6-of-12 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Spurs.

After grabbing at least seven rebounds in three straight games, Murray recorded just two on Monday. Given Sacramento’s offense, he has to do more in areas outside of scoring to provide reliable fantasy value. That hasn’t happened consistently enough, which is why Murray’s fantasy value sits well outside the top-100 in nine-cat formats.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Domantas Sabonis (SAC): Domantas Sabonis finished Monday’s loss to the Spurs with 20 points (8-of-9 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), 12 rebounds and eight assists.
item.description:
Domantas Sabonis finished Monday’s loss to the Spurs with 20 points (8-of-9 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), 12 rebounds and eight assists.

Despite foul trouble, Sabonis had one of his most productive nights of the season on Monday. The Kings center finished two assists shy of a triple-double and recorded his fourth 20-point game of the season. While establishing chemistry with rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. has been a struggle at times, Sabonis remains a valuable center in fantasy basketball, regardless of league format. The Kings play two more games in Week 6, starting with the Warriors on Wednesday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.description:
Brandin Podziemski recorded a team-high 18 points (5-of-14 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds and two assists over 37 minutes to lead the Warriors to an 88-87 win over the Celtics on Sunday.

Podziemski helped Golden State snap a five-game losing streak in a low-scoring slugfest where both teams shot below 40 percent from the floor and failed to reach 90 points. He knocked down a clutch three-pointer to put the Warriors ahead with just over two minutes left on the clock and they managed to hold off the Celtics the rest of the way. He’ll continue to play an increased role while Stephen Curry remains sidelined with a partially-torn oblique. The Warriors have a three-game week on tap that includes matchups against the Kings, Trail Blazers and Clippers.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Jayson Tatum (BOS): Jayson Tatum amassed 27 points (8-of-20 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, six assists and one steal over 38 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.
item.description:
Jayson Tatum amassed 27 points (8-of-20 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, six assists and one steal over 38 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.

Tatum scored 23 first-half points to pass Bill Russell for eighth place on the franchise’s all-time scoring list and keep Boston within striking distance. It wasn’t enough as he went ice-cold in the second half as the Celtics dropped their fourth straight game. He missed a critical free throw in the final minute before failing to nail a wide-open three-pointer that would’ve put the Celtics ahead in the final 30 seconds. He had a chance to deliver a game-winner following a huge steal by Hugo González, but missed a fadeaway over Draymond Green. The 28-year-old fantasy star has delivered second-round value this season, averaging 26.4 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.7 assists, 0.7 steals and 0.7 blocks through 15 games. The Celtics have a three-game week coming up featuring showdowns against the Wizards, Hawks and Spurs.

George Bissell

Charles Bassey chipped in 13 points (6-of-7 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists and three steals over 26 minutes in Sunday’s win over the Celtics.

Bassey delivered double-digit points for the third consecutive start shortly after Warriors head coach Steve Kerr told reporters that he wants to give Bassey an extended opportunity at center with Draymond Green moving to power forward. The decision paid dividends as Bassey came within one board of his second straight double-double. The well-traveled 26-year-old big man has looked like a viable fantasy option recently and is a worthwhile pickup in deeper formats. The Warriors have a three-game week coming up that includes matchups against the Kings, Trail Blazers and Clippers.

George Bissell

item.description:
Bam Adebayo recorded a triple-double with 24 points (8-of-11 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), 15 rebounds, 12 assists, two steals and three blocks over 37 minutes, leading the Heat to a 123-113 win over the Thunder on Sunday.

This marquee matchup lost some of its luster with generational talents Giannis Antetokounmpo (groin) and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (back, neck) both sidelined by injuries. Adebayo picked up the scoring slack with an exceptionally efficient performance, recording his ninth career triple-double, accomplishing the feat for the first time since November 29, 2024. The most impressive part of this effort was that he reached the 20-point plateau on just 11 shot attempts while earning only nine trips to the free-throw line. The Heat have a challenging three-game week ahead featuring road matchups against fellow Eastern Conference contenders in the 76ers, Knicks and Cavaliers.

Things unraveled in the third quarter as Boston went 0-for-15 from three-point range and were outscored 35-13 in the frame. Conley was one of the few bright spots in this one, coming off the bench to help lead a late comeback effort that fell just short. The 39-year-old veteran saw a huge spike in minutes with Derrick White (shoulder) sitting out and Payton Pritchard struggling to get going offensively. He was a perfect 4-of-4 from three-point range and also added three steals. He’s a non-factor for fantasy purposes at this stage of his career, but he could wind up playing an important role for Boston as a steadying presence in the postseason. item.description:

They built a 13-point lead by halftime, but went ice-cold in the third quarter, which allowed Sacramento to get back into the game.
